newsitem.title: GERMANY: German retailers happy over late Christmas buyers.
newsitem.headline: German retailers happy over late Christmas buyers.

text.p: Shoppers packed German stores on the final weekend shopping day before Christmas on Saturday, giving retailers their biggest sales of the year, industry officials said on Sunday.

Although the Christmas season has so far been disappointing, many retailers surveyed by Reuters said the final Saturday shopping day lived up to its promise and helped lift some of the disappointment over a weak autumn season.
"Saturday was the day of the decisive customer," said Julie Edelmann-Veith, a spokeswoman for the Kaufhof retailer group, the country's second largest chain of department stores.
"Three days before Christmas all those delaying their purchases finally turned up," she added. "They came in and knew what they wanted.
Edelmann-Veith said that Kaufhof's important Christmas sales period were probably slightly above 1995 levels.

Thomas Werz, spokesman for the association of German retailers (HDE) in Cologne, said the strong Saturday turnover figures should help deflect some of the disappointment from weaker sales in October and November.
"The shoppers were willing to part with some real cash," Werz said.
But many harried shoppers said they were frustrated by the enormous crowds, overwhelmed staff and at times poor service.

"It was a nice warm rain shower that we really needed," said Horst-Michael Schlonsak, managing director of a Karstadt shop in Munich, referring to the relative drought during recent December weekends.
"The place was already filled early in the morning," he said. Schlonsak said turnover this year at his central Munich shop in Germany's largest chain would be nearly 10 percent above 1995 levels.
